title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 21.

questions.question: Who stood up against Israel and provoked David to number Israel?
options: Satan
Joab
Gad
Ornan
questions.correctAnswer: Satan
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:1 states that Satan stood up against Israel and provoked David to number Israel.

questions.question: What did David command Joab and the rulers to do?
options: Number Israel from Beersheba to Dan
Attack the Philistines
Build an altar to the LORD
Gather the elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Number Israel from Beersheba to Dan
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:2 shows David commanding Joab and the rulers to number Israel from Beersheba to Dan.

questions.question: What was Joab's response to David's command to number the people?
options: He agreed immediately
He questioned why David would cause trespass to Israel
He refused to obey
He asked for more soldiers
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned why David would cause trespass to Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:3 records Joab questioning David, asking why he would be a cause of trespass to Israel by numbering them.

questions.question: Did the king's word prevail over Joab's objections?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:4 states that the king's word prevailed against Joab, so he obeyed the command.

questions.question: How many men of Israel that drew the sword were counted according to Joab's report?
options: One hundred thousand
One million one hundred thousand
Seven hundred thousand
Four hundred thousand
questions.correctAnswer: One million one hundred thousand
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:5 states that the number of men that drew the sword in Israel was a thousand thousand and an hundred thousand (1,100,000).

questions.question: Which tribes were NOT counted among the numbered men?
options: Levi and Benjamin
Judah and Benjamin
Levi and Judah
Dan and Naphtali
questions.correctAnswer: Levi and Benjamin
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:6 explains that Joab did not count Levi and Benjamin because the king's command was abominable to him.

questions.question: God was pleased with David numbering the people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:7 says God was displeased with the numbering and smote Israel as a result.

questions.question: What did David confess to God after realizing his sin?
options: I have sinned greatly and done foolishly
I will fight my enemies
I will build an altar
I will number the people again
questions.correctAnswer: I have sinned greatly and done foolishly
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:8 records David confessing his great sin and foolishness for numbering Israel.

questions.question: Who did the LORD speak to regarding David's sin?
options: Gad, David's seer
Joab, the captain
Nathan, the prophet
Ornan, the Jebusite
questions.correctAnswer: Gad, David's seer
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:9 states that the LORD spoke to Gad, David's seer.

questions.question: What choice did the LORD offer David through Gad?
options: Three years' famine, three months of defeat, or three days of pestilence
Victory, peace, or wealth
Building a temple, becoming king, or having many children
War, exile, or captivity
questions.correctAnswer: Three years' famine, three months of defeat, or three days of pestilence
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:10-12 describes the three choices the LORD offered David: three years' famine, three months' destruction by enemies, or three days of pestilence.

questions.question: Which of the following did David prefer as his punishment?
options: To fall into the hand of man
To fall into the hand of the LORD
To be destroyed by enemies
To have three years of famine
questions.correctAnswer: To fall into the hand of the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:13 shows David choosing to fall into the hand of the LORD because of His great mercy rather than into the hand of man.

questions.question: True or False: As a result of David's choice, seventy thousand men of Israel died from pestilence.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:14 records that seventy thousand men of Israel fell by pestilence sent by the LORD.

questions.question: In what order did these events happen in 1 Chronicles 21? Choose the earliest event.
options: David numbers Israel
The LORD offers David three punishments
The angel of the LORD destroys Jerusalem
David builds an altar at Ornan's threshingfloor
questions.correctAnswer: David numbers Israel
questions.explanation: According to the chapter, David first numbered Israel (verses 1-5), then the LORD offered punishments (verse 10), followed by the angel's destruction (verse 15), and finally David built the altar (verse 26).

questions.question: Joab counted Levi and Benjamin among the men who drew the sword.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:6 indicates Joab did not count Levi and Benjamin among the numbered men.

questions.question: Joab questioned David about numbering the people because he was concerned it would cause trespass to Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:3 records Joab asking why David would be a cause of trespass to Israel by numbering them.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What choice did God offer David through Gad regarding the punishment for his sin?
options: Three years' famine, three months before enemies, or three days of pestilence
Three days of darkness, three months of exile, or three years of war
Three months of drought, three years of famine, or three days of earthquake
Three years of peace, three months of harvest, or three days of joy
questions.correctAnswer: Three years' famine, three months before enemies, or three days of pestilence
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:11-12 clearly states that God, through Gad, offered David three options: three years' famine, three months of being pursued by enemies, or three days of pestilence with the angel of the Lord destroying in the land.

questions.question: How did David respond to the options given by God through Gad?
options: He chose to fall into the hands of the LORD because of His great mercy
He chose the three years' famine
He chose to be destroyed by enemies for three months
He refused to choose any option
questions.correctAnswer: He chose to fall into the hands of the LORD because of His great mercy
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 21:13, David expressed his preference to fall into the hands of the LORD, recognizing God's great mercy, rather than into the hands of men.

questions.question: What was the immediate consequence of David’s choice to fall into the hand of the LORD?
options: A pestilence fell upon Israel, killing seventy thousand men
A three-year famine began in Israel
Enemies overtook Israel for three months
The land was struck by an earthquake
questions.correctAnswer: A pestilence fell upon Israel, killing seventy thousand men
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:14 records that after David’s choice, the LORD sent a pestilence upon Israel, which resulted in the death of seventy thousand men.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about God's mercy and repentance even during judgment?
options: God saw the destruction and stopped the angel, showing mercy
God ignored the destruction and allowed it to continue
God was unaware of the destruction until it was too late
God increased the punishment because of Israel's sin
questions.correctAnswer: God saw the destruction and stopped the angel, showing mercy
questions.explanation: Verse 15 explains that as the angel was destroying Jerusalem, the LORD saw it, repented of the evil, and commanded the angel to stop, demonstrating God's mercy amid judgment.

questions.question: Where did the angel of the LORD stand when God stopped the destruction?
options: By the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite
At the gates of Jerusalem
On Mount Zion
By the tabernacle at Gibeon
questions.correctAnswer: By the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:15 states the angel of the LORD stood by the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite after the LORD commanded him to stay his hand.

questions.question: What was David's reaction when he saw the angel of the LORD with a drawn sword over Jerusalem?
options: He and the elders put on sackcloth and fell on their faces
He immediately fled from the city
He commanded the people to prepare for battle
He ignored the angel and continued his work
questions.correctAnswer: He and the elders put on sackcloth and fell on their faces
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 21:16, David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell upon their faces when they saw the angel standing with a drawn sword over Jerusalem.

questions.question: How does David demonstrate personal responsibility and intercession for the people in verse 17?
options: He claims responsibility for the sin and asks God to punish him and his family, not the people
He blames the people and asks God to punish them
He asks God to punish the priests alone
He remains silent and does not pray
questions.correctAnswer: He claims responsibility for the sin and asks God to punish him and his family, not the people
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:17 shows David acknowledging his sin in commanding the census and praying that God’s hand be on him and his father's house, sparing the people.

questions.question: What instruction did the angel of the LORD give to Gad for David in verse 18?
options: To tell David to build an altar to the LORD on the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite
To tell David to flee Jerusalem immediately
To tell David to number the people again
To tell David to prepare for war
questions.correctAnswer: To tell David to build an altar to the LORD on the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite
questions.explanation: Verse 18 instructs the angel commanding Gad to tell David to go up and set up an altar unto the LORD in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.

questions.question: What does David’s obedience to Gad’s instruction show about his character?
options: David promptly obeyed and went up to build the altar as instructed
David hesitated and disobeyed the instruction
David sent someone else to build the altar
David ignored the instruction entirely
questions.correctAnswer: David promptly obeyed and went up to build the altar as instructed
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:19 confirms David’s obedience to Gad’s message, showing his trust and submission to God's direction.

questions.question: What was Ornan doing when he saw the angel and his sons hid themselves?
options: Threshing wheat
Building an altar
Plowing the field
Tending sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Threshing wheat
questions.explanation: Verse 20 states that Ornan was threshing wheat when he saw the angel, causing him to turn back and his sons to hide.

questions.question: How did Ornan show respect to David when David approached the threshingfloor?
options: He bowed to David with his face to the ground
He ignored David and continued working
He challenged David to a contest
He fled from David
questions.correctAnswer: He bowed to David with his face to the ground
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 21:21, Ornan bowed himself to David with his face to the ground as a sign of respect.

questions.question: What lesson about integrity and generosity can be drawn from David’s interaction with Ornan about the threshingfloor?
options: David insisted on buying the threshingfloor for full price rather than accepting it for free
David took the threshingfloor without paying
David asked Ornan to build the altar for free
David did not care about the cost and accepted Ornan’s gifts
questions.correctAnswer: David insisted on buying the threshingfloor for full price rather than accepting it for free
questions.explanation: Verses 22-24 show David’s integrity as he refuses to take the threshingfloor and offerings without cost, demonstrating respect for what belongs to others and honoring God properly.

questions.question: How much did David pay Ornan for the threshingfloor?
options: Six hundred shekels of gold by weight
Three hundred shekels of silver
One thousand shekels of gold
Five hundred shekels of bronze
questions.correctAnswer: Six hundred shekels of gold by weight
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:25 records that David gave Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the threshingfloor.

questions.question: What was the result of David building the altar and offering burnt offerings on the threshingfloor?
options: God answered from heaven with fire upon the altar
The pestilence continued for another week
The angel resumed destruction
The people were further punished
questions.correctAnswer: God answered from heaven with fire upon the altar
questions.explanation: Verse 26 states that after David built the altar and made offerings, God answered him from heaven by sending fire upon the altar, showing divine acceptance.

questions.question: True or False: David could personally inquire of God at the tabernacle in Gibeon during this time because he was confident and unafraid.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:30 explains that David could not go before the tabernacle at Gibeon to inquire of God because he was afraid due to the sword of the angel of the LORD.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 21.

questions.question: What was David's response when he saw the angel of the LORD standing between earth and heaven with a drawn sword over Jerusalem?
options: He and the elders of Israel fell upon their faces in sackcloth
He immediately commanded the people to flee
He called for a fast throughout Israel
He ordered the destruction of the threshingfloor
questions.correctAnswer: He and the elders of Israel fell upon their faces in sackcloth
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:16 states that David and the elders, wearing sackcloth, fell on their faces upon seeing the angel of the LORD with a drawn sword over Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which of the following did David insist on regarding the purchase of the threshingfloor from Ornan?
options: He would pay the full price and not accept it as a gift
He accepted it as a gift from Ornan
He offered half the price
He demanded it without any payment
questions.correctAnswer: He would pay the full price and not accept it as a gift
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:24 explains that David refused to take the threshingfloor for free, insisting on paying the full price so that offerings to the LORD would not be without cost.

questions.question: What did Ornan offer David along with the threshingfloor for the burnt offerings?
options: Oxen, threshing instruments, and wheat
Only oxen
Gold and silver
Flocks of sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Oxen, threshing instruments, and wheat
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 21:23, Ornan offered David the oxen for burnt offerings, the threshing instruments for wood, and the wheat for the meat offering.

questions.question: What was the result after David built the altar and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings?
options: The LORD answered him from heaven by fire upon the altar
The people immediately rejoiced
The angel of the LORD destroyed the city
A great earthquake shook Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD answered him from heaven by fire upon the altar
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:26 indicates that after David built the altar and offered sacrifices, God responded by sending fire from heaven to consume the offerings on the altar.

questions.question: What did the LORD command the angel to do after the altar was built and offerings made?
options: Put up his sword into its sheath
Continue destroying Israel
Strike down David
Leave Jerusalem immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Put up his sword into its sheath
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:27 states that the LORD commanded the angel to sheath his sword, indicating the end of the destruction.

questions.question: Why could David not go before the tabernacle at Gibeon to inquire of God?
options: Because he was afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD
Because the tabernacle was closed
Because he was unclean
Because he was away from Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:30 explains that David was afraid to approach the tabernacle at Gibeon because of the sword of the angel of the LORD.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage also recounts David's purchase of the threshingfloor from Ornan and the building of the altar there?
options: 2 Samuel 24
Genesis 22
Exodus 25
Psalms 51
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Samuel 24
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24 recounts the same event of David purchasing the threshingfloor from Ornan and building an altar, paralleling 1 Chronicles 21:21-26.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'angel' (mal'ak) in this chapter, and how does it relate to the role of the figure sent to destroy Israel?
options: Messenger; it emphasizes the angel as God's envoy executing judgment
Warrior; it highlights the angel as a soldier of Israel
King; it shows the angel as a ruler over Israel
Priest; it indicates the angel as a mediator between God and man
questions.correctAnswer: Messenger; it emphasizes the angel as God's envoy executing judgment
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'mal'ak' means 'messenger,' indicating the angel’s role as God's envoy who carries out divine judgment, as seen in 1 Chronicles 21:15 where the angel destroys but is stopped by God.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 1 Chronicles 21:21-30 to highlight the transition from judgment to mercy?
options: Chiasm
Alliteration
Paradox
Simile
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The passage employs a chiasm structure, moving from the appearance of judgment (angel with sword) to mercy (altar and cessation of plague), as seen in 1 Chronicles 21:21-30.

questions.question: What was David's plea when he recognized he had sinned by numbering Israel, according to 1 Chronicles 21:17?
options: Let your hand be on me and my father's house, but not on your people
Destroy all Israel as punishment
Allow Joab to atone for the sin
Remove the angel from Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Let your hand be on me and my father's house, but not on your people
questions.explanation: In 1 Chronicles 21:17, David asks God to punish him and his family rather than the people, acknowledging his sin in commanding the census.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the three punishments offered by the LORD to David through Gad?
options: Ten years of peace
Three years' famine
Three months of destruction by enemies
Three days of the LORD's pestilence
questions.correctAnswer: Ten years of peace
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:12 lists the three options given to David: famine, destruction by enemies, or pestilence, but not ten years of peace.

questions.question: Cross-reference question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's mercy shown to David despite his sin in numbering Israel?
options: Romans 5:20
Matthew 27:46
John 3:16
Revelation 21:4
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 5:20
questions.explanation: Romans 5:20 discusses how where sin increased, grace abounded much more, echoing God's mercy to David despite his sin in 1 Chronicles 21:8-13.

questions.question: What historical or cultural significance does the threshingfloor of Ornan have in the context of the ancient Near East?
options: It was a recognized sacred site suitable for altar construction
It was a common marketplace for trade
It was a military fortress
It was a royal palace
questions.correctAnswer: It was a recognized sacred site suitable for altar construction
questions.explanation: Threshingfloors in the ancient Near East were often elevated, open spaces suitable for building altars, making Ornan's threshingfloor an appropriate site for David's altar as in 1 Chronicles 21:18-26.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 21:6, Joab included the tribes of Levi and Benjamin in the census count.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 1 Chronicles 21:6 explicitly states that Joab did not count Levi and Benjamin because the king's word was abominable to him.

questions.question: True or False: The plague sent upon Israel as a result of David's sin killed seventy thousand men.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:14 confirms that the LORD sent a pestilence upon Israel, and seventy thousand men died.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is demonstrated by God's displeasure and punishment of Israel after David's census?
options: The doctrine of Divine justice and holiness
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of the Trinity
The doctrine of eternal security
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of Divine justice and holiness
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:7 shows God's displeasure and subsequent judgment upon Israel, revealing His justice and holiness in responding to sin. God's righteous anger is a foundational aspect of His character confirmed elsewhere, e.g., Romans 1:18.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 21:13 reveal an attribute of God in David's appeal during the plague?
options: God's mercy and compassion
God's omniscience
God's immutability
God's wrath
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy and compassion
questions.explanation: David appeals to God's mercy, indicating he trusts in God's compassionate nature despite judgment, as stated in 1 Chronicles 21:13. This aligns with God's portrayal as merciful in Exodus 34:6.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do verses 22 and 24 teach about the nature of worship and sacrifice?
options: Worship must be sincere and costly, not taken without payment
Worship is purely ceremonial without moral requirement
Sacrifice is optional and symbolic only
God accepts gifts regardless of the giver's heart
questions.correctAnswer: Worship must be sincere and costly, not taken without payment
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:22 shows David requesting to buy the threshing floor for full price, and verse 24 confirms he refuses to offer sacrifices without cost, teaching the doctrine that true worship requires sincere and costly offerings, consistent with Hebrews 9:22.

questions.question: What does the narrative arc of the angel of the LORD standing with a drawn sword over Jerusalem in 1 Chronicles 21:16 signify in redemptive history?
options: God's imminent judgment and the need for atonement
God's abandonment of His people
The final defeat of Israel
The establishment of a new covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God's imminent judgment and the need for atonement
questions.explanation: The angel with a drawn sword symbolizes God's pending judgment on Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 21:16), highlighting humanity's need for atonement, a theme fulfilled ultimately in Christ's sacrifice (Isaiah 53).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted by His sending an angel to destroy Jerusalem, then relenting when He saw the altar built by David?
options: God's patience and responsiveness to repentance
God's wrath without mercy
God's unpredictability
God's sovereignty limited by human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God's patience and responsiveness to repentance
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:15 shows God repenting of the evil when He saw the altar, demonstrating His patience and merciful responsiveness to David's sacrifice and repentance, consistent with Joel 2:13.

questions.question: From 1 Chronicles 21:5-6, what does the exclusion of Levi and Benjamin from the census reveal about God's people and the nature of sin?
options: That not all within Israel were counted as part of the fighting force due to the abomination of the king's command
That Levi and Benjamin were not part of Israel
That the census was a perfect representation of God's people
That sin does not affect God's people
questions.correctAnswer: That not all within Israel were counted as part of the fighting force due to the abomination of the king's command
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 reveal Joab's refusal to count Levi and Benjamin because he considered the king's command sinful, illustrating how sin disrupts the relationship within God's people and affects their standing.

questions.question: What does David's prayer in 1 Chronicles 21:17 teach about substitutionary atonement?
options: David offers himself and his household to bear the punishment instead of the people
David requests the people to be punished for his sin
David ignores the consequences of his actions
David blames the people for his sin
questions.correctAnswer: David offers himself and his household to bear the punishment instead of the people
questions.explanation: In 1 Chronicles 21:17, David takes responsibility and asks God to lay the punishment on him and his house rather than the people, foreshadowing substitutionary atonement, a key doctrine fulfilled in Christ (Isaiah 53:4-6).

questions.question: How does the episode of David building an altar at Ornan's threshing floor (verses 18–26) relate to the doctrine of sanctification and divine provision?
options: It shows God providing a holy place for worship and purification after judgment
It indicates God's rejection of physical altars
It shows that sanctification happens without cost
It teaches that worship is unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God providing a holy place for worship and purification after judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 18–26 describe David erecting an altar at Ornan's threshing floor, marking the provision of a sanctified place for atonement and worship, illustrating sanctification's necessity following sin and judgment.

questions.question: What combined theological truth do 1 Chronicles 21:9-14 present about God's sovereign judgment and human choice?
options: God offers judgment options, but humans must choose and accept responsibility
God imposes judgment without warning or choice
Humans can evade God's judgment by ignoring Him
Judgment is random and unrelated to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God offers judgment options, but humans must choose and accept responsibility
questions.explanation: Verses 9-14 show God presenting David with three judgment options and David choosing one, emphasizing human responsibility within divine sovereignty, consistent with Deuteronomy 30:19.

questions.question: What does the sceptical objection that 'God’s repentance in 1 Chronicles 21:15 shows He is fallible' misunderstand about divine nature, and what does the passage actually teach?
options: God’s 'repentance' is anthropopathic language expressing His relational mercy and not fallibility
God literally changes His mind like humans
God is inconsistent and makes mistakes
God is limited by human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s 'repentance' is anthropopathic language expressing His relational mercy and not fallibility
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21:15 states God 'repented,' but this anthropopathic expression reveals God's merciful character toward repentant people, not fallibility. This aligns with theological affirmations of God's immutability (Malachi 3:6).

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 21:28-30 illustrate the tension between the presence of God and human fear in the redemptive narrative?
options: David feared approaching the tabernacle because of the angel’s sword, showing reverence and awareness of divine holiness
David boldly approached the tabernacle without fear
The tabernacle was irrelevant to God's presence
David's fear shows a lack of faith
questions.correctAnswer: David feared approaching the tabernacle because of the angel’s sword, showing reverence and awareness of divine holiness
questions.explanation: Verses 28-30 show David’s fear to approach the tabernacle due to the angel's sword, highlighting the holiness of God’s presence and human fear before divine judgment, a theme consistent with Isaiah 6:5.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about the nature of sin and leadership is evident from 1 Chronicles 21:1-4 regarding David's numbering of Israel?
options: Sin can be provoked by Satan even in godly leaders, and human sin has corporate consequences
Leaders cannot sin
Satan has no influence over human decisions
Sin only affects individuals, not nations
questions.correctAnswer: Sin can be provoked by Satan even in godly leaders, and human sin has corporate consequences
questions.explanation: Verses 1-4 reveal Satan provoking David to sin by numbering Israel, showing even godly leaders are vulnerable and that sin affects the whole nation, consistent with corporate responsibility in Scripture (Exodus 32:30-35).

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 21:26 teach about God’s acceptance of worship and the role of divine response in sanctification?
options: God answered from heaven by fire, confirming acceptance and sanctifying the altar
God ignored the altar and offerings
Worship without fire is acceptable
Sanctification is unrelated to divine response
questions.correctAnswer: God answered from heaven by fire, confirming acceptance and sanctifying the altar
questions.explanation: Verse 26 states God responded with fire on the altar, indicating divine acceptance of worship and sanctifying the place, highlighting the importance of God's response for sanctification, consistent with Leviticus 9:24.

questions.question: How does the exchange between David and Ornan in verses 23-25 teach about the principle of costly redemption in salvation theology?
options: David insists on paying full price, illustrating that redemption requires a cost
Salvation can be freely taken without cost
Ornan refuses any payment, so redemption is free
David steals the land for the altar
questions.correctAnswer: David insists on paying full price, illustrating that redemption requires a cost
questions.explanation: David's refusal to accept Ornan's gift and his insistence on paying six hundred shekels (vv. 23-25) illustrates the biblical principle that redemption and worship must involve a cost, reflecting doctrines of substitutionary atonement (1 Peter 1:18-19).

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine communication and human mediation is found in 1 Chronicles 21:9 and 1 Chronicles 21:18?
options: God speaks through prophets like Gad to direct human action in response to sin
God remains silent and does not guide people
Humans must act without divine instruction
Prophets act independently of God's will
questions.correctAnswer: God speaks through prophets like Gad to direct human action in response to sin
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 18 show God communicating with David through the prophet Gad, demonstrating the biblical principle of prophetic mediation guiding God's people in correction and worship (Amos 3:7).
